text: You are treated as a critical part of the Dusk Research Group's operations. A dedicated port dock, full laboratory access, and exotic military equipment is all yours. Science teams often try to hire your services or invite you to sit in during meetings and give your valuable insights. You even have a personal comm line to the Director, should it be needed.

Administrators of the DRG have given you their trust and offer wide access to the reseach group's labs. Scientists often try to stop you to ask for information about happenings in fringe space, and special military hardware is also available for you to purchase should you desire.

The Dusk Research Group considers you as a serious partner, and agents of all walks treat you with respect. More over, you’ve been granted cursory access to the research wing of DRG's facilities, and are permitted to purchase some special equipment.

You possess upgraded status as a 'DRG Independent Associate' at this time. You are permitted to use priority queues and Acquisitions Agents always treat you with smiles and respect. Pragmatically you have no special access however, and more private dealings remain off limits to you.
You are offered the same polite service as other potential business partners of the Dusk Research Group. What the DRG administration thinks of you personally is an unknown quantity however.

Despite being treated in a formal manner, the Dusk Research Group obviously considers you to be of low regard. Acquisitions Agents no longer give their full range of services, and Relations personnel make you jump through bureaucratic hoops far more often than others.

Your status as a potential business partner has been declared null and void by the Dusk Research Group, and port agents will no longer offer to trade with you. Security patrols strictly follow protocol and will harass you at the slightest infraction, although will not engage in combat unless necessary.

You are considered as one of the many adversarial elements opposing the Dusk Research Group. Acquisitions Agents are prohibited from conducting business with you, and Relations and Enforcer fleets will pursue and attack you when able.

The Dusk Research Group administration considers you an imminent threat to their operations. Significant resources have been pulled from other projects and allocated to aid in your destruction. Your name and face appear in security briefings frequently.
Internal Affairs has flagged your $shipOrFleet as having seen a blacksite, and assigned a dedicated officer to monitor your actions.

The Persean Separatists claim you as one of their own in all but name. Citizens see you as a beacon of freedom, officials trust you as a steadfast ally. You are given much leeway, and it is not uncommon to be invited to business dealings and offered exclusive treatment at port.

You have become a reliable ally to the Persean Separatists. The polity on Sedna has made public note of your relationship, and many citizens view you with admiration. Officers and dealers make a point of treating you well, trusting you with restricted information and hardware.

The Separatists have come to trust you as a friend of the people, and are spared the typical frosty attitude common place in the colonies. Officials occasionally overlook the more pedantic rules, and traders offer rarer goods for purchase at your request.

People in Separatists territory have tacitly accepted your presence among the colonies. Polite nods and a willingness to speak to you are fairly commonplace, but any type of favored treatment is still denied to you.
The Persean Separatists have no strong opinions about you, which is to say they generally view you and your $shipOrFleet with the same suspicion as the rest of the sector.

You are a total outsider to the Separatists. Few will have words with you, even fewer will offer aid. Traders are wary to conduct business with your $shipOrFleet, and often demand perfect paperwork before even considering the possibility, not to mention the constant harassment from patrols.

Negative stories about your $shipOrFleet have spread through the union, the name "$playerName" is frequently mixed with choice curses and maledictions. The militia raise their guard whenever your transponder is detected, and public traders refuse to trade out of solidarity to the populous.

The Persean Separatists have marked you as an actively hostile actor in their space. Militia forces watch for any sign of your $shipOrFleet, and public bulletins have been distributed asking the population to report sightings of you.

The entirety of the Separatists have rallied against you and everything you represent. Citizens enthusiastically volunteer for militia service to fight against your $shipOrFleet. Moreover, even the fractious polity on Sedna have agreed to fund substantial bounties, payable on your destruction.

You possess the flagship of the Separatist founder, The Speedwell. Though many would prefer it returned to the hands of the PSM proper, the citizenry generally tolerate you bearing the symbol of their independence.

You bear the flagship of the Separatist founder, The Speedwell. Most, if not all citizens consider an outsider holding such a symbol to be appalling, and are undoubtedly petitioning the president to take action to reclaim it.

text:
Once long lost and thought to be destroyed, it now sits before you. The significance lost on you, the one time Separatist proudly explains the vessels mythos:

The Speedwell is, or rather was, the personal flagship of the founder and first leader of the Separatists. Referred to as the 'General' in current cycle, many particular details of his person have apparently been obscured through time, resulting in the General becoming more a mythological character than a concrete person.

None the less, you gather he was not unlike yourself, ambitious, effective, and capable of great feats of command seemingly through will alone.

Obscure lore aside, the Speedwell itself served both as a formidable command vessel, and even more importantly a symbol of Separatist independence. Its loss coincided with the stagnation of the Separatist movement, ending with their current position in the sector today.

Your ops chief, annoyed with the explanation causing delay, coughs loudly and looks to you for confirmation. Words are unneeded, the question is clear: send in the salvors?

Ops nods, then turns to bark commands on the salvors' command frequency.

Junior officers scurry to cajole crew prepping cargo-handling drones while Sensors puts one analysis team on careful outward watch and another on the hulk to ensure there are no surprises.   

Within short minutes, the first salvors dock their open-vacuum shuttle frames and utility drones at various entry points identified along the vessel's massive hull.

Ops gives the go-order.

In short order, salvage crews enter into the Speedwell, and begin spreading throughout the hull.

The process is surprisingly fast, far faster than typical ops of this size.

Reports begin flowing in, offering explanation to this anomaly.

The hull, though battered and somewhat degraded, is in acceptable operational condition, certainly no worse than any independent expedition fleet.The reactor and even the power runs are fully functional.

Plasma torches and pry bars hang on their belt hooks, unused, as your crew's passage through the hulk is simple as walking through doors.

Even the flight deck, which has sustained the worst damage, remains in a serviceable state despite being pockmarked by meteoroid impacts.

Ops continues to enforce their typical strict protocol, though it is obvious that the salvors have relaxed somewhat after realizing the ship is not on the verge of spontaneous detonation.

The air of calm sharply declines as they make their way into the crew quarters. It becomes quickly apparent that there is not a single sign of life, and not in the usual sense either. The deck is entirely devoid of evidence from the previous crew.

There is no debris in the corridors, no personal belongings in the bunks, not even a single dead spacer in a busted vac-suit slumped in a corner. 

Nothing. 

It looks like it just came off a nanoforge line, ready to be christened.

The systems logs are empty as well. Not even junk data left in the gaps of deleted files. Just endless streams of neat zeros.

Whatever secrets of past the Speedwell held, it seems they vanished along with the crew.

The work continues apace, albeit with more caution and the occasional mutterings of a salvor ritual to guard against the unknown.

None the less, it soon comes to an end.

"$PlayerSirOrMadam," the chief barks, "report is ready for you."

You nod, and take the datapad from them.

Still, someone went through the trouble to configure the mirrors in this manner, desperate measures perhaps.

text:
An image appears on-screen, and the whole bridge goes silent. Even Operations, typically unflappable, halts their regimental shouting.

Lying in a corner surrounded by debris, in a damaged vac-suit, is a dead body unlike any other in the Sector.

An alien.

Not the lower kind one might find out there on a habitable world, but a walking, talking, vac-suit wearing alien. Or at least, this one was once walking and talking, before being burned through by blaster fire.

It isn't long before the body is transferred to the med-bay and the CMO begins an autopsy, while you watch from the observation gallery.

An entire gamut of examinations are performed, and though your fleet lacks the facilities necessary to analyze more esoteric details, a conclusion is soon reached.

This creature is shockingly 'normal' for an alien life form. Nominal brain size, limb function, immune system, and even vocal chord structure are within human approximation.

In fact, it would likely be able to live alongside humans without much issue, in terms of life-support at least. The happenings on the station suggest whatever it was, it didn't like people very much.
These revelations further bring an eerie air to the corpse, making it as though a man, once familiar, had been cut apart and reassembled into a freakish skin suit, or furred suit in this case.

Your admin staff are already taking action to prevent information leaks, though rumors are bound to spread eventually.

More pressing is the question of how to proceed, as it's hard to imagine whom, if anyone, has knowledge on this matter.

"Salvage teams have finished their prelim', ready to begin transfers on your order."

text:
You join your technology officer and engineering chief in a small briefing room overlooking the shop bay dedicated to what has been euphemistically dubbed "special salvage".

Haz-suited technicians attend to the containment machinery, stepping over coils of tube and wire. A mess of makeshift components were pulled from the common microforge libraries then torn apart and re-engineered to operate in this unusual, even extraordinary, application.

Engineering wears a frown, tapping a TriPad as they observe the ongoing work. Tech can barely contain their excitement. 

"$PlayerSirOrMadam," they say in unison at your arrival.

"Living metal!" Tech exclaims.

"More specifically, it seems to be a distributed synthetic intelligence suspended in a ferro-fluid," the tech officer almost seems giddy.

Engineering interrupts with a scowl, not sharing in Technologies' enthusiasm, "Nanites captain, they're nanites."

"Bah, it's so much more then mere nanites," Tech retorts, more to Engineering than to you.

Both officers straighten, remembering whom they are speaking with, "Yes, ah, apologies $playerSirOrMadam," Tech nods.

"In short, this fluid has some form of autonomy and can interact with and control machinery, and is capable of self replication," Tech glances at Engineering, "not unlike nanites."

options: drgBiometalOptSelF:"Show me what you can do."

text:
"We frankly don't know, captain," your engineering chief makes a show of standing while speaking, it appears they've been arguing about this.

"Well, um." Tech passes a look of consternation back toward your chief engineer.

"In truth, I could not say, precisely. And unfortunately we're not equipped to perform a full scientific investigation. Clearly it is a part of, or more likely it is the... the animating force behind the hostile fleet which we bested."

"Extremely," Tech answers. "Assuming you find the right buyer, as without a way to control it..."

"It's dangerous," Engineering says. "There's a reason AI tech is banned, for better or for worse. A weapon you can't control is just a hazard to every-"

"-Yes, yes," Tech interrupts. "As with any applied technology, sufficiently powerful, it could... $playerSirOrMadam. To answer your query, yes, extremely valuable."

"Highly likely," your technology officer exchanges another look with Engineering. "If a programming method can be determined, the use cases are numerous. In my professional opinion."

"Going with generalization of 'nanites', they could be used for things like repair, structural modification, and even autonomous control. In theory anyway."

Your chief engineer steps forward. "With a big emphasis on if, captain. Put enough of this stuff together and it just 'wakes up' and goes wild. All it would take is one accident and..."

"Look, I did concede you were correct about th-" Tech catches your expression and shuts up, putting on a deferential look.

Engineering presents you a TriPad with test data on it, "It's difficult, but sustained heat can cause it to harden and delaminate, which renders it, well, dead I suppose."

Tech speaks up, "Also the stuff is sensitive to strong electrical pulses, it won't exactly be destroyed, but it interrupts the networking part of its, em, mind, and..." A pause for a few moments.

"Well, basically it'll 'go to sleep' for a while." Both officers look to each other and nod in agreement.

"It's risky, and I personally wouldn't recommend it, but," the chief engineer glances at Tech, "with enough precautions..."

"We can't use it at its full potential, $playerSirOrMadam, however," your technology officer hands you a set of schematics.

You quickly recognize the standardized diagrams of bulkheads and superstructures, now intermixed with strange control systems, EM amplifiers, and hydraulic pumps.
"$PlayerSirOrMadam," they say once more in unison.

//Submit to judgment, let your//your officers massacred!//You are advised to disengage or we//We fight and we die for the Domain//Damage teams report to//to all ships retreat//inside! It's inside the ship//ships and cargo are ours//

The communications are nearly incomprehensible, save for what sounds like the collective shouting and anguish of innumerable spacers.

The link is filled with noise, the hissing and growl of synthetic signals clawing at the safety thresholds.

With a wince, your comms officer freezes the output and purges the buffer.
